<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Thassilo M. Schiepanski
</span></span></div>

<figure id="fig1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2508.04412v4/0-downsampling.png" id="g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:332/220;" width="332" height="220" alt="[Uncaptioned image]">
</figure>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_section" style="font-size:120%;">1  Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Web-based user interfaces have traditionally been human-centric and, consequently, developed primarily around visual output and manual input. Artificially intelligent agents that autonomously browse the web on behalf of humans (hereafter referred to as web agents) have been a longstanding subject of research <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amandi and Armentano (2004)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gur et al. (2024a)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al. (2024)</a></cite>. Such agents are constrained to interact with human-facing user interfaces, as application programming interfaces are often unavailable, incomplete, or restricted <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Booking.com (2024)</a></cite>. Conventional AI agents have largely relied on heuristic search over a formal model of the problem domain <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Poole and Mackworth (2017)</a></cite>. Because web application UIs are highly complex and diverse, constructing a model adequate for human-centric web browsing is non-trivial. Large language models have recently enabled a new approach to building web agents. In this paradigm, an LLM serves as a reasoning backend: given serialised UI state (hereafter referred to as a snapshot), it is expected to suggest input for advancing a specified web browsing task <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deng et al. (2023)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2024a)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">1.1  Problem</h3>

<div id="S1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Web browser automation frameworks expose perception and actuation interfaces to capture output and send input, respectively <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">SeleniumHQ (2026)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Microsoft (2026)</a></cite>. A central problem in developing web agents (hereafter used synonymously with LLM-based web agents) is context engineering <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mei et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anthropic (2025)</a></cite>: how best to facilitate an LLM’s interpretation of a web page UI to elicit accurate input actions, each specified by a type and a target (e.g., <span id="S1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">click</span> on a specific <span id="S1.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">button</span>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">GUI (graphical UI) snapshots, i.e., screenshots, emulate what humans see when viewing a web page. Image input to LLMs is downsampled, which decouples input byte size from input token count <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2025a)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2025b)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2025c)</a></cite>. As a result, GUI snapshots of representative real-world web pages fit comfortably within the context window of many frontier LLMs today <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2025d)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anthropic (2024)</a></cite>. LLM vision capabilities still lack pixel precision as image downsampling does not systematically preserve actionable elements. For that reason, state-of-the-art web agents have increasingly been premised on grounded GUI snapshots – screenshots enhanced with visual cues that survive downsampling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Müller and Žunič (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Browser Use (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2023)</a></cite> (see <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A GUI Snapshot Examples ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Attachment <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></span></a>). Text-based snapshots – DOM snapshots in particular – present a viable alternative to GUI snapshots. The DOM is a web browser’s runtime model of a web page, and HTML is the DOM’s canonical serialisation format <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">WHATWG (2025b)</a></cite>. LLMs have demonstrated the ability to interpret HTML and even navigate UIs indirectly encoded as HTML <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gur et al. (2022)</a></cite>. However, DOM snapshots of representative real-world web pages routinely exceed the context window of many LLMs today <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Webfuse (2025)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Enabling DOM snapshots for use with web agents therefore motivates pre-processing techniques, analogous to image pre-processing that LLM providers already implement <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2025a)</a></cite>. Such techniques must reduce a snapshot’s size without compromising its utility as input to a web agent’s LLM backend. Preserving a valid DOM is desirable, ultimately, to allow further processing, such as translation to an accessibility tree. Naïve truncation of the serialised DOM removes actionable elements indiscriminately and breaks HTML syntax.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">1.2  Contributions</h3>

<div id="S1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this work, we propose <span id="S1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">D2Snap</span>, an algorithm for downsampling the DOM. Intended as a pre-processing technique for use with web agents, it locally consolidates DOM nodes such that the output’s utility as a snapshot is largely preserved – trading fidelity for size. Crucially, it remains a valid DOM.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate D2Snap through a minimal, snapshot-variant agent (<span id="S1.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">GPT-4o</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2025d)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2024b)</a></cite> backend) on web browsing tasks derived from <span id="S1.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Online-Mind2Web</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xue et al. (2025b)</a></cite>. To avoid subjective judgement, we handcraft a multimodal snapshot dataset along verified solution trajectories (52 snapshots, 18 trajectories), annotated with ground-truth action targets.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Raw DOM snapshots exceed the model’s context window (<math id="S1.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128\times 10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128\times 10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens) in 42% of the cases, at a mean model context utilisation of 109%. All snapshots of our reference configuration – low retention of elements, high retention of attributes, moderate retention of text – fit, at a utilisation of 16.5% against 3.0% for a grounded GUI snapshot (Set-of-Mark) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Müller and Žunič (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2023)</a></cite> baseline. Its 73% success rate is not significantly different from the baseline’s 67% rate (<math id="S1.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+5.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>5.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+5.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, 95% CI <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-13.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>13.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-13.6</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+26.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>26.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+26.0</annotation></semantics></math>%pt; McNemar, <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.47" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.47</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.47</annotation></semantics></math>), excluding a deficit (one-sided 95%) beyond 11%pt. Our results support that HTML conveys salience: flattening the DOM to text with inlined actionable elements significantly underperforms our reference (<math id="S1.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-26.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>26.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-26.9</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.002</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.002</annotation></semantics></math>). Baseline snapshots without images attain 62% (<math id="S1.SS2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-5.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-5.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt; <math id="S1.SS2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.37" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.37</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.37</annotation></semantics></math>), indicating that image input adds little to snapshot utility.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_section" style="font-size:120%;">2  D2Snap</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Downsampling is a technique to reduce data through local, lossy consolidation, such that encoded features are largely preserved <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gonzalez and Woods (2018)</a></cite>. A digital image can be locally consolidated by averaging an <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-tile of pixels – the depicted object would remain recognisable <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">LeCun et al. (1998)</a></cite>. We transfer this principle to the DOM: it can analogously be locally consolidated by merging <math id="S2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-subtrees of nodes into a single ’average’ node. What constitutes a feature thereby depends on the intended purpose of the downsampled DOM; in our case, features are implied by the downsampled DOM’s utility as a snapshot for a web agent’s LLM backend. A gradual increase of the downsampling ratio should yield a gradual DOM reduction. Since HTML lexemes have unbounded length, however, monotonic size reduction is a strong aim, and linear size reduction a weak, best-effort aim.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">2.1  Algorithm</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose D2Snap <span id="S2.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(<span id="S2.SS1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline ltx_font_italic">D</span><span id="S2.SS1.p1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ownsample <span id="S2.SS1.p1.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">D</span>OM <span id="S2.SS1.p1.1.1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_underline">Snap</span>shots</span>)</span> – an informed algorithm for downsampling the DOM, designed to preserve (A) its utility as a web agent snapshot, and (B) syntactic validity. It figuratively averages redundant nodes of three types: elements, attributes and text <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">WHATWG (2025a)</a></cite>. To control downsampling per type, we introduce three parameters over the unit interval: the ratios <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{e}</annotation></semantics></math> for elements and <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> for text, and the discarding threshold <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> for attributes (<math id="S2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{e},r_{a},r_{t}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{e},r_{a},r_{t}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, 1 <math id="S2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\equiv" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≡</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\equiv</annotation></semantics></math> maximal downsampling). <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Example DOM Snapshots ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Attachment <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></span></a> lists examples of D2Snap-downsampled DOM snapshots.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The DOM is a tree structure <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">WHATWG (2025a)</a></cite> – size reduction lies in reducing the hierarchy rendered by nested elements. D2Snap averages elements by merging adjacent elements. The parameter <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{e}</annotation></semantics></math> governs the removed height fraction to target a DOM height of <math id="S2.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max(1,\lceil h(\mathrm{DOM})\cdot(1-r_{e})\rceil)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌈</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>DOM</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌉</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max(1,\lceil h(\mathrm{DOM})\cdot(1-r_{e})\rceil)</annotation></semantics></math>: merge levels are distributed evenly by a Bresenham gate <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bresenham (1965)</a></cite>. A virtual root node is implied, exempt from consolidation, to admit full DOM flattening. A merge describes substituting the deeper candidate element by its own children. This concept of averaging rests on two assumptions: (1) structural segregation decreases with depth, and (2) most attributes are reflexive or forward-transitive (e.g., <span id="S2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">id</span>, or <span id="S2.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">hidden</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">WHATWG (2025b)</a></cite>, respectively). The converse of (2) does not hold -- an invisible element can have a visible parent. As downsampling trades fidelity for size, we accept that attributes might become fuzzy or be swallowed<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
              
              
              
            Pruning ineffective (e.g., hidden) subtrees from the DOM beforehand would mitigate attribute semantics drift.</span></span></span>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="LST1" class="ltx_float ltx_lstlisting">
<div id="LST1.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_language_pseudocode ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx1" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">switch</span><span id="lstnumberx1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Class</span><span id="lstnumberx1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ELEMENT_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">):</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx2" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">case</span><span id="lstnumberx2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Class</span><span id="lstnumberx2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">.</span><span id="lstnumberx2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ACTIONABLE</span><span id="lstnumberx2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">:</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx3" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">break</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx4" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">case</span><span id="lstnumberx4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Class</span><span id="lstnumberx4.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">.</span><span id="lstnumberx4.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">TEXT_FORMATTING</span><span id="lstnumberx4.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">:</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx5" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">TEXT_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><math id="lstnumberx5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leftarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;" mathbackground="#FAFAFA" stretchy="false">←</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leftarrow</annotation></semantics></math></span><span id="lstnumberx5.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx5.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Markdown</span><span id="lstnumberx5.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx5.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ELEMENT_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx5.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">)</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx6" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Replace</span><span id="lstnumberx6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ELEMENT_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx6.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">,</span><span id="lstnumberx6.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">TEXT_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx6.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">)</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx7" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">break</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx8" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">default</span><span id="lstnumberx8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">:</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx9" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">d</span><span id="lstnumberx9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><math id="lstnumberx9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leftarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;" mathbackground="#FAFAFA" stretchy="false">←</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leftarrow</annotation></semantics></math></span><span id="lstnumberx9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx9.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Depth</span><span id="lstnumberx9.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><sub id="lstnumberx9.7.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="lstnumberx9.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">frozen</span></sub></span><span id="lstnumberx9.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx9.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ELEMENT_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx9.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">)</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx10" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">    </span><span id="lstnumberx10.2" class="ltx_text </div>
<div id="lstnumberx11" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">      </span><span id="lstnumberx11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Replace</span><span id="lstnumberx11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx11.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ELEMENT_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx11.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">,</span><span id="lstnumberx11.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx11.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ELEMENT</span><span id="lstnumberx11.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><sub id="lstnumberx11.8.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="lstnumberx11.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Children</span></sub></span><span id="lstnumberx11.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">)</span>

</div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float">Listing 1: </span>D2Snap consolidates element nodes by substituting an element with its children, distributed evenly through an <math id="LST1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;" mathbackground="#FAFAFA">r</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;" mathbackground="#FAFAFA">e</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{e}</annotation></semantics></math>-ratio Bresenham gate. The root level is exempt, retaining a valid DOM at <math id="LST1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{e}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;" mathbackground="#FAFAFA">r</mi><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;" mathbackground="#FAFAFA">e</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;" mathbackground="#FAFAFA">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#FAFAFA;" mathbackground="#FAFAFA">1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{e}=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Absolute measures: actionable elements are preserved as-is, text-formatting elements are translated to Markdown.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Actionable Elements.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Elements that semantically afford actionability represent atoms of the DOM-encoded UI – that is, triggers for UI state transitions. Element consolidation idiomatically transfers the concept of downsampling to the DOM. However, as we design D2Snap for use with web agents, we strictly exclude actionable elements from consolidation. For atomicity, actionable elements, such as buttons, should not inflate with content, particularly from parents. Also, actionable elements presumably hold no deep container substructure, so their exclusion only marginally compromises the targeted DOM height.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Text-Formatting Elements.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As an absolute size reduction measure, we include translation of HTML-serialised text-formatting elements to token-efficient Markdown equivalents <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gruber (2004)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">GitHub (2019)</a></cite>. Most aggressive HTML syntax downsampling (<math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{e}=r_{a}=1,r_{t}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{e}=r_{a}=1,r_{t}=0</annotation></semantics></math>) then produces a Markdown representation with inlined actionable elements – an input-aware alternative to existing Markdown snapshots <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ango (2025)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#LST1" title="Listing 1 ‣ 2.1 Algorithm ‣ 2 D2Snap ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Listing <span class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></span></a> is a pseudocode description of D2Snap’s element node sub-procedure.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsubsection">2.1.1  Attribute Nodes</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Attributes are leaf nodes attached to elements, so reducing the DOM in elements implies reducing attributes. There is no evident analogue of local consolidation for attributes, e.g., regarding centrality. To avoid unconditioned survival of heavy attributes, D2Snap discards attributes whose relevance falls below <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>. We are aware of no authoritative such relevance scoring, so we define it as a heuristic represented through an empirical parameter <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> – a lookup table (see <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C LLM-Elicited1 Attribute Scoring ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Attachment <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></span></a>) or scoring function (<math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>). If <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> not only scores attributes by relevance, but also calibrates those scores against global attribute frequency, the threshold <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> functions as a latent downsampling ratio – ideally governing removal of the <math id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>-fraction of attributes from the DOM. <a href="#LST2" title="Listing 2 ‣ 2.1.1 Attribute Nodes ‣ 2.1 Algorithm ‣ 2 D2Snap ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Listing <span class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></span></a> is a pseudocode description of D2Snap’s attribute node sub-procedure.</p>
</div>
<figure id="LST2" class="ltx_float ltx_lstlisting">
<div id="LST2.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_language_pseudocode ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64,aWYgJFxtYXRoY2Fse0F9JChBVFRSSUJVVEVfTk9ERSRfe1xtYXRocm17TmFtZX19JCkgPCAkcl9hJDoKICBSZW1vdmUoQVRUUklCVVRFX05PREUp" download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx13" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">if</span><span id="lstnumberx13.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><math id="lstnumberx13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span id="lstnumberx13.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx13.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ATTRIBUTE_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx13.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><sub id="lstnumberx13.6.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="lstnumberx13.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Name</span></sub></span><span id="lstnumberx13.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">)</span><span id="lstnumberx13.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx13.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">&lt;</span><span id="lstnumberx13.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx13.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><math id="lstnumberx13.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{a}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span id="lstnumberx13.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">:</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx14" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx14.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Remove</span><span id="lstnumberx14.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx14.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ATTRIBUTE_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx14.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">)</span>
</div>
</div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float">Listing 2: </span>D2Snap removes attributes that score below the threshold <math id="LST2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="LST2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> is calibrated against global attribute frequency, <math id="LST2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> functions as a latent downsampling ratio.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsubsection">2.1.2  Text Nodes</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Text nodes embed natural language into the DOM. D2Snap consolidates text by reducing its size at the sentence level <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rai and Borah (2021)</a></cite>. Of the many text-summarisation techniques available, D2Snap uses the <span id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">TextRank</span> algorithm <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mihalcea and Tarau (2004)</a></cite> for a generalist setup, pruning the floored <math id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> fraction of sentences with the lowest centrality within the text body, whilst preserving their original order<span id="footnote2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">2</span>
                
                
                
              TextRank on sentences is meaningless for few sentences. For short texts, it can be substituted, e.g., by truncation.</span></span></span>. Single-sentence text nodes, as common for buttons or links, are hence retained. <a href="#LST3" title="Listing 3 ‣ 2.1.2 Text Nodes ‣ 2.1 Algorithm ‣ 2 D2Snap ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Listing <span class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></span></a> is a pseudocode description of D2Snap’s text node sub-procedure.</p>
</div>
<figure id="LST3" class="ltx_float ltx_lstlisting">
<div id="LST3.2" class="ltx_listing ltx_lst_language_pseudocode ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx15" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SENTENCES</span><span id="lstnumberx15.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx15.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><math id="lstnumberx15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leftarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leftarrow</annotation></semantics></math></span><span id="lstnumberx15.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx15.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Tokenize</span><span id="lstnumberx15.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx15.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">TEXT_NODE</span><span id="lstnumberx15.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><sub id="lstnumberx15.8.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="lstnumberx15.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">TextContent</span></sub></span><span id="lstnumberx15.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">)</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx16" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx16.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SENTENCES</span><span id="lstnumberx16.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><sub id="lstnumberx16.2.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="lstnumberx16.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ranked</span></sub></span><span id="lstnumberx16.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx16.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><math id="lstnumberx16.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leftarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leftarrow</annotation></semantics></math></span><span id="lstnumberx16.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx16.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">TextRank</span><span id="lstnumberx16.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><math id="lstnumberx16.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}_{\textrm{Sentence}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>Sentence</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{\textrm{Sentence}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span id="lstnumberx16.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx16.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SENTENCES</span><span id="lstnumberx16.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">)</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx17" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx17.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SENTENCES</span><span id="lstnumberx17.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><sub id="lstnumberx17.2.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="lstnumberx17.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">selected</span></sub></span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx18" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx18.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">  </span><span id="lstnumberx18.2" class="ltx_text id="lstnumberx18.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">[0</span><span id="lstnumberx18.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"> <figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float">Listing 3: </span>D2Snap consolidates text nodes on a sentence level: text is tokenised into sentences and ranked by centrality using the TextRank algorithm. The lowest-ranking <math id="LST3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> fraction is discarded; surviving sentences are re-emitted to the text node in their original order. At least one sentence is always retained.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#A4" title="Appendix D D2Snap ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Attachment <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></span></a> displays a full pseudocode description of D2Snap.</p>

</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_section" style="font-size:120%;">3  Evaluation</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our experimental setup to evaluate D2Snap isolates the snapshot representation as the independent variable, and its utility as LLM input as the dependent variable. Our principal research questions are:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S3.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RQ 1.</span> Do D2Snap-downsampled DOM snapshots fit comfortably within a frontier LLM’s context window? We operationalise a comfortable fit as mean model context utilisation (CU<sub id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">%</span></sub>) of at most 20%; leaving headroom for two-snapshot history (<math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times</annotation></semantics></math> 20%), additional history context (<math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> 10%) and a system prompt (20%).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RQ 2.</span> Do D2Snap-downsampled DOM snapshots allow a frontier LLM to suggest input action targets that advance real-world web browsing tasks?</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">3.1  Evaluation Dataset</h3>

<figure id="S3.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2508.04412v4/3-annotated-trajectory.png" id="S3.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/91;" width="476" height="91" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>Annotated solution trajectory of UI states encoded as GUI snapshots from our dataset on <span id="S3.F1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">drugs.com</span> for the task: <span id="S3.F1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“Check the interaction between Novolin N and Novolin R”</span>. Coloured bounding boxes represent annotated action targets. A group of equally coloured boxes forms a coherent target set. A web agent must interact with all elements of a single coherent target set to transition across the UI state trajectory. Our dataset contains full-page GUI snapshots.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To this end, we construct a dedicated snapshot dataset, sourced from Online-Mind2Web <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xue et al. (2025b)</a></cite>. We randomly sample 6 easy, 6 medium, and 6 hard web browsing tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In a first pass, a human (non-author) is asked to solve each sampled task, for which we collect a solution trajectory of snapshots<span id="footnote3" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">3</span>
              
              
              
            Snapshots are taken before each input <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xue et al. (2025a)</a></cite>.</span></span></span>. Each snapshot is a triple of independent representations: a DOM snapshot, a GUI snapshot, and a grounded GUI snapshot, emulating the Set-of-Mark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2023)</a></cite> approach of <span id="S3.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Browser Use</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Müller and Žunič (2024)</a></cite>. We verify all trajectories via <span id="S3.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">WebJudge</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">NLP (2025b)</a></cite>; all 18 trajectories passed verification. The resulting dataset contains a total of 52 tuples of tasks and snapshot-triples – each snapshot along a trajectory is treated as an independent sub-task.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In a second pass, two software engineers (non-authors) independently annotate every snapshot triple, identifying all coherent sets of input action targets. A coherent action target set is a minimal set of UI elements that requires input (e.g., clicking or typing) to advance a related web browsing task, i.e., transition between adjacent, encoded UI states. A snapshot may admit multiple coherent target sets (e.g., a redundant link in the <span id="S3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">header</span> and the <span id="S3.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">footer</span>). An annotation takes the form of bounding-box coordinates for a GUI snapshot, supplemented with a numerical identifier (if available) for a grounded GUI snapshot, and a unique CSS selector for a DOM snapshot. For assessing snapshot utility, we do not verify action target arguments, nor order within coherent action target sets. Annotations (<math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>) yield an inter-annotator agreement of F1 = 0.89<span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">4</span>
              
              
              
            Pairwise F1 between both annotators’ action target sets (<math id="footnote4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|A|=471" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>471</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|A|=471</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="footnote4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|B|=499" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>499</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|B|=499</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="footnote4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|A\cup B|=538" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>∪</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>538</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|A\cup B|=538</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="footnote4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|A\cap B|=432" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>∩</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>432</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|A\cap B|=432</annotation></semantics></math>). Two annotated action targets match if: (1) they share the same snapshot, (2) they share the same representation, and (3), depending on the representation, their bounding boxes overlap by <math id="footnote4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{IoU}\geq 0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>IoU</mtext><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{IoU}\geq 0.75</annotation></semantics></math>, their numeric IDs are equal, or their CSS selectors resolve to the same element.</span></span></span>. Given high agreement, we take either annotator’s targets to be valid and build the evaluation reference from the union<span id="footnote5" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">5</span>
              
              
              
            Two matched bounding boxes are united as the minimal rectangle enclosing both.</span></span></span>, i.e., ground-truth action targets against which LLM-suggested targets can be matched. <a href="#S3.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 3.1 Evaluation Dataset ‣ 3 Evaluation ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Figure <span class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></span></a> shows an example annotation for a trajectory of GUI snapshots. <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Annotated Dataset Entry ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Attachment <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></span></a> excerpts a dataset reference annotation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">3.2  Evaluation Framework</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The evaluation of snapshot representations is designated to deploy a web agent across each tuple from the dataset, once per representation. The web agent LLM backend’s response is counted as a success if the suggested action targets form a superset of any coherent target set in the reference<span id="footnote6" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">6</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">6</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">6</span>
              
              
              
            Elements are compared with slight tolerance: for GUI snapshots, we inflate referenced bounding boxes by 10 pixels to each side; for DOM-based snapshots, we additionally accept a referenced node’s parent. The latter accommodates input event bubbling behaviour <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stchur and Steiner (2021)</a></cite>. Although expressed in different units, both tolerances absorb representation-specific ambiguity: pixel-level annotation jitter (GUI), and handler uncertainty (DOM).</span></span></span><span id="footnote7" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">7</span>
              
              
              
            The agent could trivially satisfy the success criterion by excessively suggesting action targets. We mitigate such degenerate suggestions by rejecting target sets exceeding <math id="footnote7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times</annotation></semantics></math> the size of the largest coherent reference set. The buffer accounts for additional, non-interfering action targets (e.g., an info-box). Across our experiments, the ceiling was reached at most twice per snapshot representation.</span></span></span>. At the aggregate level, the evaluation success rate is computed over all 52 task-snapshot tuples per representation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">3.3  Experimental Setup</h3>

<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2508.04412v4/3-success-rate-mean-tokens.png" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:452/170;" width="452" height="170" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>Agent success rates and mean token sizes across snapshot representations plotted as a bar chart. Grounded GUI snapshots (GUI<sub id="S3.F2.6" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.F2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">gr.</span></sub>) represent the baseline (67%, 95% Wilson CI: 54% to 78%). 42% of raw DOM snapshots exceeded the model’s context window (GPT-4o, <math id="S3.F2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128\times 10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128\times 10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens). Every D2Snap-downsampled snapshot fits. Success with D2Snap-based representations is not significantly different from the baseline (e.g., D2Snap<sub id="S3.F2.7" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.F2.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.9,.3,.6</span></sub>, 73%; <math id="S3.F2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+5.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>5.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+5.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, 95% CI <math id="S3.F2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-13.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>13.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-13.6</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.F2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+26.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>26.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+26.0</annotation></semantics></math>%pt; McNemar, <math id="S3.F2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.47" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.47</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.47</annotation></semantics></math>). Grounding text alone (<del id="S3.F2.8" class="ltx_del downdiagonalstrike"><span id="S3.F2.8.1" class="ltx_text">GUI</span></del><sub id="S3.F2.9" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.F2.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grounded</span></sub>) reaches 62% (McNemar, <math id="S3.F2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.37" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.37</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.37</annotation></semantics></math>).</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We deploy a minimal web agent – merely a model with a snapshot-variant system prompt – to attribute performance differences to snapshot representations. As the backend, we choose GPT-4o (<span id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gpt-4o-2024-11-20</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2025d)</a></cite>), a multimodal, general-purpose model, with a context window of <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128\times 10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128\times 10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens (<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\equiv 100\%\ \text{CU}_{\%}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>≡</mo><mn>100</mn><mo rspace="0.500em">%</mo><mtext>CU</mtext><msub><mrow></mrow><mo>%</mo></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\equiv 100\%\ \text{CU}_{\%}</annotation></semantics></math>)<span id="footnote8" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">8</span>
              
              
              
            For reproducibility, agent response temperature is fixed at <math id="footnote8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>. Results per snapshot representation are averaged across three runs; booleans are averaged by majority.</span></span></span>. Rather than establishing heuristic attribute scoring manually, we elicit it directly from the model, independently of the dataset, which presupposes the model’s capacity to interpret HTML semantics – the enabling assumption of LLM-based DOM interpretation. Additionally, we write a system prompt template instructing the model to suggest all action targets that advance a given task on a web page encoded by a given snapshot, and substitutions specific to each snapshot representation. With DOM snapshots, for instance, element targeting is described by means of CSS selectors. <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C LLM-Elicited1 Attribute Scoring ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Attachment <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></span></a> records our experimental attribute scoring lookup table, including eliciting model prompts. <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Evaluation System Prompt ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Attachment <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></span></a> records the exact system prompt templates used in our experiments.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Snapshot Representations.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As the baseline snapshot technique, we adopt grounded GUI snapshots, as implemented by <span id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Browser Use</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Browser Use (2025)</a></cite> following Set-of-Mark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2023)</a></cite> (A). Our evaluation compares the baseline against its grounding text alone, i.e., without the image (B), raw GUI snapshots (C), and raw DOM snapshots (D). It covers a range of D2Snap-downsampled DOM snapshots compiled from raw DOM snapshots from the dataset (E, F), including a linearised Markdown representation with inlined actionable HTML (G). <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A GUI Snapshot Examples ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Attachment <span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></span></a> shows an example of a GUI snapshot and its equivalent grounded GUI snapshot. The evaluated snapshot representations are referred to by class notation:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">

<td id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-top:2.5pt;padding-bottom:2.5pt;"><span id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.5.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}_{r_{e},r_{a},r_{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{r_{e},r_{a},r_{t}}</annotation></semantics></math></span></td>
