<td id="S3.T1.2.21.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_b" style="padding-top:0.85pt;padding-bottom:0.85pt;"><span id="S3.T1.2.21.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">3.51, 66.81</span></td>
<td id="S3.T1.2.21.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_b" style="padding-top:0.85pt;padding-bottom:0.85pt;"><span id="S3.T1.2.21.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">16.4</span></td>
<td id="S3.T1.2.21.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_b" style="padding-top:0.85pt;padding-bottom:0.85pt;"><span id="S3.T1.2.21.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">0.18</span></td>
<td id="S3.T1.2.21.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_b" style="padding-top:0.85pt;padding-bottom:0.85pt;"><span id="S3.T1.2.21.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">2.22</span></td>
<td id="S3.T1.2.21.10" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_b" style="padding-top:0.85pt;padding-bottom:0.85pt;"><span id="S3.T1.2.21.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">0.21</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>Agent evaluation results across snapshot representations over <math id="S3.T1.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>52</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=52</annotation></semantics></math> annotated snapshots, averaged across three runs at temperature <math id="S3.T1.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>: agent task success rates with marginal 95% Wilson intervals, which are per representation, not a basis for pairwise comparison. Mean byte and token sizes with token percentiles (5th, 95th; wide, as individual web page sizes vary). Mean model context utilisation (CU<sub id="S3.T1.24" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.T1.24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">%</span></sub>, GPT-4o, <math id="S3.T1.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128\times 10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128\times 10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens). Mean snapshot size ratio against the mean raw DOM snapshot from the dataset (<math id="S3.T1.m42" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{Raw}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>Raw</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{Raw}}</annotation></semantics></math>). Mean latency normalised to the lowest recorded value (<del id="S3.T1.25" class="ltx_del downdiagonalstrike"><span id="S3.T1.25.1" class="ltx_text">GUI</span></del><sub id="S3.T1.26" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.T1.26.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grounded</span></sub>) with 1 SEM. Grounded GUI snapshots (GUI<sub id="S3.T1.27" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.T1.27.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grounded</span></sub>) represent the baseline. 42% of raw DOM snapshots exceeded the context window. Success with D2Snap-based representations is not significantly different from the baseline (e.g., D2Snap<sub id="S3.T1.28" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.T1.28.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.9,.3,.6</span></sub>, <math id="S3.T1.m46" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+5.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>5.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+5.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, McNemar, <math id="S3.T1.m47" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.47" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.47</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.47</annotation></semantics></math>), nor with grounding text alone (<del id="S3.T1.29" class="ltx_del downdiagonalstrike"><span id="S3.T1.29.1" class="ltx_text">GUI</span></del><sub id="S3.T1.30" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.T1.30.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grounded</span></sub>, McNemar, <math id="S3.T1.m49" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.37" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.37</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.37</annotation></semantics></math>).</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2508.04412v4/3-tokens-9-3-6.png" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/316;" width="476" height="316" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Ordered token sizes for each D2Snap-downsampled DOM from the dataset, produced by <span id="S3.F3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.F3.3.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.F3.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.9,.3,.6</span></sub></span>. All snapshots fit within the model’s context window (GPT-4o, <math id="S3.F3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.28\times 10^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.28</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.28\times 10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens), at a mean utilisation of 16.5% and a maximum of 54%. 50% are below <math id="S3.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Raw DOM snapshots (<span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DOM</span>) exceed the model’s context window in 42% of the cases, at a mean CU<sub id="S3.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">%</span></sub> of 109%. Even at moderate downsampling ratios, every D2Snap-downsampled snapshot fits, and 13 of 15 assessed configurations have at most 20% CU<sub id="S3.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">%</span></sub> (<span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RQ 1</span>)<span id="footnote11" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">11</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">11</span>
              
              
              
            We estimate LLM input tokens from serialised byte size. We map targets between original DOM and downsampled counterparts by assigning unique data attributes to the DOM. These are excluded from size measurements, as they stem from an opinionated mapping approach – a source map would not affect snapshots directly. To not introduce bias, these attributes are applied to every element and values are incremental integers.</span></span></span>. At a CU<sub id="S3.SS4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">%</span></sub> of 16.5%, our reference configuration <span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.p1.1.6.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.9,.3,.6</span></sub></span> achieves a success rate of 73%, which is not significantly different from the baseline (<span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GUI<sub id="S3.SS4.p1.1.7.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grounded</span></sub></span>) rate of 67% (<math id="S3.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+5.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>5.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+5.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, 95% CI <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-13.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>13.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-13.6</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+26.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>26.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+26.0</annotation></semantics></math>%pt; McNemar, <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.47" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.47</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.47</annotation></semantics></math>) – excluding a deficit (one-sided 95%) beyond 11%pt (<span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RQ 2</span>). Text-linearised representations (<span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.p1.1.9.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1.0</span></sub></span>, <span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.p1.1.10.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">MD</span></sub></span>) attain the lowest success rates among D2Snap configurations, underperforming our reference configuration significantly (42%, <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-30.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>30.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-30.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&lt;0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&lt;0.001</annotation></semantics></math>; 46%, <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-26.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>26.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-26.9</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, <math id="S3.SS4.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.002</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.002</annotation></semantics></math>). <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3.4 Experimental Results ‣ 3 Evaluation ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Table <span class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></span></a> compares all evaluated snapshot representations on agent success, snapshot size, and LLM backend latency. <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.3 Experimental Setup ‣ 3 Evaluation ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Figure <span class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></span></a> visualises success rate and token count among key representations. <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.4 Experimental Results ‣ 3 Evaluation ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Figure <span class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></span></a> plots token counts of every output of our reference D2Snap configuration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At a success rate of 2%, LLM vision capabilities evidently lack pixel-precision. Grounding is therefore necessary to make GUI snapshots effective (<span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GUI<sub id="S3.SS4.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grounded</span></sub></span>, 67%). However, we detect no significant difference when using the grounding text without screenshots as standalone snapshots (<del id="S3.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_del downdiagonalstrike ltx_font_bold"><span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text">GUI</span></del><sub id="S3.SS4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">grounded</span></sub>); the agent attains a success rate of 62% (<math id="S3.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-5.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-5.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, 95% CI <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-18.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>18.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-18.0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+7.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>7.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+7.1</annotation></semantics></math>%pt; McNemar, <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.37" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.37</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.37</annotation></semantics></math>), which suggests that the text, rather than the image input, carries most utility-inherent features.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Ablation Study.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We infer the impact on snapshot utility of each D2Snap parameter by raising a single parameter to 0.9 (high) from an otherwise uniform 0.3 (low). Against the uniform <span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.3</span></sub></span> reference (71%, <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{Raw}}=0.24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>Raw</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{Raw}}=0.24</annotation></semantics></math>), this directionally yields: (A) <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{e}</annotation></semantics></math> – low retention of elements (hierarchy) – reduces size by 18% at 73%, so structural segregation can be traded almost freely; (B) <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> – low retention of attributes – reduces size by 53%, the largest saving of any parameter, but drops to 67%, indicating that attributes add most to utility; and (C) <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> – low retention of text – neither reduces size (1.9%) nor changes success (71%) noticeably. The embedded text consolidation technique (we deployed TextRank) narrows down to a semantic-to-verbosity optimisation problem. Notably, retaining HTML at low fidelity (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.6</span></sub></span>, 73%) outperforms full removal of HTML (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1.0</span></sub></span>, 42%; <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+30.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>30.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+30.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, McNemar, <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p&lt;0.001" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p&lt;0.001</annotation></semantics></math>) – supporting the use of DOM snapshots over abstract text-based snapshot representations. Retaining text at full length (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">MD</span></sub></span>, 46%) does not measurably change utility over discarding it (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1.0</span></sub></span>; <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+3.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>3.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+3.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.32</annotation></semantics></math>), suggesting that natural language text verbosity contributes little to a DOM snapshot’s utility.</p>
</div>

<tr id="S3.T2.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T2.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l" style="padding-top:0.85pt;padding-bottom:0.85pt;"></td>
<th id="S3.T2.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column" style="padding-top:0.85pt;padding-bottom:0.85pt;"><span id="S3.T2.2.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Tokens <span id="S3.T2.2.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:88%;">(<math id="S3.T2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times 10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times 10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>)</span></span></th>
<th id="S3.T2.2.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column" style="padding-top:0.85pt;padding-bottom:0.85pt;"><math id="S3.T2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{Raw}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathsize="0.800em" mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi mathsize="0.800em">Raw</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{Raw}}</annotation></semantics></math></th>
<th id="S3.T2.2.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column" style="padding-top:0.85pt;padding-bottom:0.85pt;"><math id="S3.T2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathsize="0.800em" mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math></th></tr>

The progression is strictly monotonic (Spearman <math id="S3.F4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=-1.000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.000</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=-1.000</annotation></semantics></math>). Over the operating range <math id="S3.F4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, it fits <math id="S3.F4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta}_{\mathrm{Raw}}=0.311-0.226\,r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>Raw</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.311</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>0.226</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta}_{\mathrm{Raw}}=0.311-0.226\,r</annotation></semantics></math> (Pearson correlation <math id="S3.F4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.965" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.965</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.965</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.F4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}=0.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.93</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}=0.93</annotation></semantics></math>). The drop from <math id="S3.F4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.F4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8</annotation></semantics></math> is due to the elimination of the high-frequency <span id="S3.F4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">class</span> attribute. The size progression on the first snapshot from the dataset resembles the trend.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Range Study.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">D2Snap’s output ranges from the original HTML (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_sub">0</sub></span>) to fully flattened content – virtually Markdown with inlined actionable elements (<span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">D2Snap<sub id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1.0</span></sub></span>). We record the uniform configurations <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=r_{e}=r_{a}=r_{t}\in\{0.1,\ldots,1.0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=r_{e}=r_{a}=r_{t}\in\{0.1,\ldots,1.0\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Size reduction is strictly monotonic across this range (Spearman <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho=-1.000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.000</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho=-1.000</annotation></semantics></math>), satisfying our strong aim. It further approximates a constant reduction rate: a linear regression of the mean size ratio against <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> over the operating range fits <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta}_{\mathrm{Raw}}=0.311-0.226\,r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>Raw</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.311</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>0.226</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta}_{\mathrm{Raw}}=0.311-0.226\,r</annotation></semantics></math> (Pearson correlation <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.965" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.965</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.965</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}=0.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.93</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}=0.93</annotation></semantics></math>), satisfying our weak aim. The drop from <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8</annotation></semantics></math> stands out: it is due to the <span id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">class</span> attribute <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">WHATWG (2025b)</a></cite>, which our experimental attribute scoring places at <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.77</annotation></semantics></math> and which is therefore discarded once <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds that score. Aligned with prior expectation, this is a high-frequency attribute. Restricting the regression to <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\in\{0.1,\ldots,0.7\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\in\{0.1,\ldots,0.7\}</annotation></semantics></math>, below that threshold, yields a closer fit of <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\Delta}_{\mathrm{Raw}}=0.285-0.146\,r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>Raw</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.285</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>0.146</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\Delta}_{\mathrm{Raw}}=0.285-0.146\,r</annotation></semantics></math> (Pearson correlation <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.993" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.993</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.993</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}=0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.99</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}=0.99</annotation></semantics></math>). <a href="#S3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Ablation Study. ‣ 3.4 Experimental Results ‣ 3 Evaluation ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Table <span class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></span></a> reports mean snapshot token counts and size ratios across the recorded range; <a href="#S3.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Ablation Study. ‣ 3.4 Experimental Results ‣ 3 Evaluation ‣ Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_bold">Figure <span class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></span></a> plots the size ratios against the regressions.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_section" style="font-size:120%;">4  Related Work</h2>

<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Context Engineering.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Input token efficiency has been approached with increasing web agent specificity: LLMLingua <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al. (2023)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al. (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pan et al. (2024)</a></cite> discards low-saliency tokens by perplexity in continuous natural language prose – a noteworthy alternative to our TextRank component of D2Snap. Set-of-Mark prompting augments a GUI snapshot with visual cues <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2023)</a></cite>, which has influenced state-of-the-art production agents such as <span id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Browser Use</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Browser Use (2025)</a></cite>. Token-extraction and -stripping approaches reduce HTML directly, yet apply uniform transformations that disregard differential DOM node semantics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chang et al. (2006)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gupta et al. (2003)</a></cite>. Closest to our work, structured-text representations serialise the page directly: most obviously, the accessibility tree <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Boxhall et al. (2016)</a></cite> derived from the DOM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al. (2024)</a></cite>. Markdown constitutes an orthogonal representation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ango (2025)</a></cite>. Such representations typically follow element extraction – surfacing a designated subset of elements for translation. Element extraction has built on above-outlined transformations, but also on LLM inference, such as relevance ranking or predictors conditioned on prior actions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gur et al. (2024b)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deng et al. (2023)</a></cite> – at the cost of added latency. In contrast, D2Snap downsamples the full DOM under an explicit fidelity-size trade-off, preserving features that constitute or discriminate action targets across the entire representation at a controllable ratio, and emitting a valid DOM.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Web Agents.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A growing body of work has proposed architectures for generalist, LLM-based web agents <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al. (2023)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gur et al. (2024a)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al. (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al. (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al. (2023)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Müller and Žunič (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI (2025e)</a></cite> – based on DOM, GUI or hybrid snapshots. A parallel line of work has focused on web agent evaluation: Mind2Web <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deng et al. (2023)</a></cite> introduced a static dataset of web browsing tasks to assess web agent success. Online-Mind2Web <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xue et al. (2025b)</a></cite> is a smaller-scale derivative targeting execution on the live web; WebVoyager <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al. (2024)</a></cite> likewise targets the live web. These datasets are designed to capture actual web browsing journeys rather than final results <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">NLP (2025a)</a></cite>. The evaluation of snapshot utility in isolation, however, has received comparatively little attention – generalist web agent evaluation results merely allow indirect assessment of snapshot representations. Our work closes this gap, presenting a static dataset to assess different snapshot representations. Our related experimental framework is designed to assess the impact of a specific snapshot representation independently of individual web agent logic. It does, moreover, not require human or AI judgement (e.g., WebJudge <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">NLP (2025b)</a></cite><span id="footnote12" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">12</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">12</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">12</span>
              
              
              
            We utilised WebJudge once to validate task solution UI state trajectories in our dataset. It is not used in our repeatable experimental framework.</span></span></span>), as it defines objective rules to determine success.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_section" style="font-size:120%;">5  Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">DOM snapshots – if not for their excessive LLM input footprint – represent a compelling alternative to GUI snapshots. In this paper, we introduced DOM downsampling: trading DOM fidelity for size, whilst preserving a valid DOM.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">5.1  Contributions</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose D2Snap – an algorithm to downsample the DOM, premised on preserving actionability and actionability-discriminating features, intended as a size-reducing pre-processing technique for DOM snapshots used with web agents. On D2Snap-downsampled DOM snapshots, a minimal, snapshot-variant web agent (GPT-4o, context size: <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128\times 10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>128</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128\times 10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> tokens) achieves a web browsing task success rate that is not significantly different from that of a grounded GUI snapshot baseline (<math id="S5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+5.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>5.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+5.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, 95% CI <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-13.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>13.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-13.6</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+26.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>26.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+26.0</annotation></semantics></math>%pt), excluding a deficit (one-sided 95%) beyond 11%pt, at a mean model context utilisation of 16.5%. Every D2Snap-downsampled snapshot fits within the context window; 42% of raw DOM snapshots exceed it. We further detect no significant difference in success between grounded GUI snapshots and the grounding text alone (<math id="S5.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-5.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-5.8</annotation></semantics></math>%pt, 95% CI <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-18.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>18.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-18.0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+7.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>7.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+7.1</annotation></semantics></math>%pt), which suggests that image input contributes little to snapshot utility. Ablation on success indicates that retention of attributes contributes most to snapshot utility. In turn, low retention of element hierarchy is sufficient (73%), yet full removal of HTML is not (46%). We show that D2Snap downsamples strictly monotonically and approximately linearly across its operating range (linear regression: slope <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.226" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.226</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.226</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}=0.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0.93</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}=0.93</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The data and code repository associated with this paper is publicly available at <a href="https://github.com/webfuse-com/D2Snap" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">github.com/webfuse-com/D2Snap</a>, mirrored at <a href="https://github.com/t-ski/D2Snap" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">github.com/t-ski/D2Snap</a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">5.2  Limitations</h3>

<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our evaluation dataset has a modest size (<math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>52</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=52</annotation></semantics></math>), which limits the precision of our estimates. Our reference configuration was selected among the results. It ties with three further configurations at the highest observed success rate, and among those exhibits the lowest context utilisation – a criterion independent of success. Our evaluation relies exclusively on GPT-4o, so results should be read as indicative of snapshot utility for few real-world-representative web pages and a highly capable model. Elicited once, our attribute scoring is best regarded as a model-informed prior.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Integration.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Web browsers strictly constrain DOM-access to cross-origin documents embedded via the <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">iframe</span> element <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">WHATWG (2025a)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">WHATWG (2025b)</a></cite>. Whilst GUI snapshots are able to capture what is visually rendered within embedded documents’ viewports <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Microsoft (2025)</a></cite>, DOM snapshots are not. The same limitation holds for graphics-based applications via the <span id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">canvas</span> element <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">WHATWG (2025b)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">5.3  Future Work</h3>

<section id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Automated, systematic exploration of the downsampling parameter space – across a broader range of frontier LLMs and web applications – would identify optimal configurations and establish generalisability of the approach. Moreover, we elicited attribute scoring heuristics from a single model under a generic eliciting prompt; future work could investigate alternative elicitation strategies.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Integration.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since D2Snap preserves a valid DOM, it can serve as an intermediate size control measure within a snapshot pipeline. In a subsequent processing step, for instance, the downsampled DOM could be translated to an accessibility tree. In a preceding step, certain subtrees could be pruned, e.g., due to invisibility or redundancy.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Beyond Web Agents.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The applicability of DOM downsampling is not limited to the web agent domain. Other domains that might benefit from the concept include accessibility, content summarisation, and UI testing – all of which rely on the DOM.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
</section>

<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">A.1  GUI Snapshot</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">A GUI snapshot corresponds to a screenshot.</span></p>
</div>

<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">A.2  Grounded GUI Snapshot</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">A grounded GUI snapshot corresponds to a GUI snapshot (image) enhanced with visual cues – to bridge the lack of LLM vision pixel-precision. Visual cues are coloured bounding boxes identified by numerical indices (Set-of-Mark). The grounding (text) describes actionable elements associated with these identifiers providing (tag) name and text contents.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A1.SS2.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="853.16" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 704.33 853.16" width="704.33"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,853.16) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#D4E6FF;" fill="#D4E6FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 853.16 L 704.33 853.16 L 704.33 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#EEF5FF;" fill="#EEF5FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.69 0.69 L 0.69 852.47 L 703.64 852.47 L 703.64 0.69 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 14.01)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:57.33em;--ltx-fo-height:59.81em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" height="830.07" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 827.61)" width="793.29"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 13.08)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:37.65em;--ltx-fo-height:7.69em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.11em;font-size:10pt;" height="107.93" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 106.39)" width="520.97"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A3.p1.pic1.p1.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:37.65em;">
<span id="A3.p1.pic1.p1.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p1.pic1.p1.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">For each standard HTML attribute: Score its UI-features, i.e., its semantics in the inherent user interface (‘S’), using a ratio scale on the unit interval <math id="A3.p1.pic1.p1.pic1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. Subsequently calibrate these scores against the global frequency of each attribute so that, in a DOM representative of an average document, the fraction of attribute occurrences with a score of at most ‘s’ is approximately s, for every s in <math id="A3.p1.pic1.p1.pic1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. Respond with a list of tuples (attribute, S).

<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Evaluation System Prompt</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:241.5pt;height:68.1pt;vertical-align:-61.8pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(0.0pt,0.0pt) scale(1,1) ;">
<p id="A6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text">
<span id="A6.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:241.5pt;">
<span id="A6.p1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.p1.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">To control the system prompt used in our evaluation, we define a generic template. The template contains variable tags (<span id="A6.p1.1.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lstlisting ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">\{\{<span id="A6.p1.1.1.1.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>&lt;<span id="A6.p1.1.1.1.1.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">TAG</span>&gt;<span id="A6.p1.1.1.1.1.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>\}\}</span>) for each snapshot specific part of the prompt. Below are the template, and specific substitutes per snapshot class.</span></span>
</span></span></p>
</span></div>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">F.1  Template</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A6.SS1.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="33.24" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 704.33 33.24" width="704.33"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,33.24) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#D4E6FF;" fill="#D4E6FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 0 L 0 33.24 L 704.33 33.24 L 704.33 0 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#EEF5FF;" fill="#EEF5FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.69 0.69 L 0.69 32.55 L 703.64 32.55 L 703.64 0.69 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15.01 14.01)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:720.52em;--ltx-fo-height:0.56em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" class="ltx_minipage" height="10.15" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 7.69)" width="57.33em"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><pre id="A6.SS1.p1.pic1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
# Identity

You are an AI agent that solves web-based tasks on behalf of a human user.

&gt; Assume that today is July 16, 2025.

# Instructions

The user provides you with a web-based task, and serialised state of the web application to solve the task with.
A task may be iterative, so it may not be possible to solve the task completely, but only partially with the given state.

Based on the state representation, your goal is to suggest all elements required to interact with in order to solve the task.
It is important that the list of elements corresponds to a complete interaction trajectory. High precision when
referencing target elements is key in order to be able to reproduce the interactions on the respective user interface.

## Input

### Task

The web-based task is denoted with the prefix ‘TASK:‘, e.g. "TASK: Show 4-star hotels in Amsterdam".

### Snapshot

<span id="A6.SS1.p1.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">{{ SNAPSHOT_DESCRIPTION }}</span>

# Output

Follow these rules when considering an element for interaction:

- In case there are multiple trajectories to solve the task, rank them in memory according to human-readability
  and choose the highest ranked alternative
- If there are alternative elements per trajectory which seem to do the same thing, choose the most expressive alternative
- Suppose there are only point and click actions, so never imply any other interaction
- Try not to over-suggest, i.e., suggest only mandatory elements to solve the task with

## Schema

<span id="A6.SS1.p1.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">{{ SCHEMA_DESCRIPTION }}</span>

# Examples

Consider the web-based task "TASK: Calculate the sum of 2 and 3.".

&lt;user_query&gt;
  TASK: Calculate the sum of 2 and 3.
&lt;/user_query&gt;

&lt;user_query&gt;
  <span id="A6.SS1.p1.pic1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">{{ EXAMPLE_SNAPSHOT }}</span>
&lt;/user_query&gt;

&lt;assistant_response&gt;
  <span id="A6.SS1.p1.pic1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">{{ EXAMPLE_RESPONSE }}</span>
&lt;/assistant_response&gt;
</pre></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection">F.3  Grounded GUI</h3>

      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
